This app got a significant update a year or so ago, I think to switch the underlying code base or platform to the more modern one for iOS. While that change should’ve been largely under the hood, in practice it seems to have introduced several bugs that have caused a significant downgrade in user experience.

The two main ways the update has degraded the user experience are download failures and not retaining user changes to the order in custom playlists.

The automatic downloads are frequently not fully automatic, as in, a podcast episode released overnight will appear in my playlist but often will not start downloading until I’ve opened the app. Downloads also often fail inexplicably, requiring the user to manually tap to download the episode. There is no particular rhyme or reason to which episodes fail, as it happens seemingly randomly even when I open the app and have multiple episodes from the same podcast downloading at once. It’s a crapshoot whether they all download successfully without a failure.

The other very annoying bug is that if I’ve reordered the episodes in a custom playlist, the app will often undo that change, requiring me to again drag the episodes to restore my custom order.

I don’t recall either of these bugs appearing before the major update, and as it’s been I think a year or more since then, it’s quite disappointing that these bugs haven’t been fixed.

title.label: Best Pod Player of ALL Players

content.label: After needlessly suffering the shocking lack of any useful features and attempting to quell the growing frustration over the constant interruptions of the poorly matched mandatory advertisements forced upon users, I finally abandoned Apple’s standard podcast player and have been using Overcast ever since. I absolutely LOVE everything about Overcast. I appreciate the intuitive nature of its interface, along with the simplicity of its useful organizational features. I can arrange my pods using the Playlists feature which allows one to apply a range of colors to categorize the wide-ranging and eclectic subject matter of my favorite shows (Daily Favs, Politics, Constitutional Law, Skeptical/Freethinking, Parenting, Ye Olde Timey Radio, etc). Each playlist can be updated using quick ‘click/apply’ functions (Star, Add/Remove to Playlist, etc), and can then be easily edited using drag-and-drop and/or swipe to prioritize listening. You can customize the way each individual Podcast plays: • set the playback speed (1x to 5x+) • boost voice (helps equalize voice levels of participants speakers); • reduce pauses (to close up unedited gaps in chatting) and; • set the show start and end time to skip over lengthy intros, commercials, and/or closing credits (for example, one of my fav political pods takes more than 5.5 minutes to get from the start of the show…with the intro music, to the show overview [which you can read in the Show Notes] through the first 60 second sponsor commercial, then through detailed introductions of his three guest panelists. So I set the start time at 05:30 which puts me right at the start of the first segment. My FAVORITE FEATURE is Playback Speed which can be adjusted at increments from .5 to 2x, while the pod is playing. Some of my other fav features of Overcast include: 1) applying a “Star” to an episode (allows me to go back through the lengthy episode lists of my favorite podcasts, some going back as far as 2010 with more than 700 episodes - and ‘Star’ specific episodes that I want to listen to but don’t want to presently download); and 2) Skip Ads, simply by hitting the customizable forward button. While there are auto-inserted ads in some podcast shows, there are NO mandatory non skippable ads in any of the pods that I listen to. It’s lovely to not have my shows interrupted by ‘Must Listen’ annoying and irrelevant ads. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!! You’ll love it!

If you like podcasts and care about a good listening experience, I cant recomend Overcast enough.
